title: Cold rebuild: Merge
summary: Rebuild Merge from memory, no hints.

steps.title: Cold rebuild
body: Time to prove a piece stuck. You built **Merge** in *Merge sort*. Now write it again from an
**empty editor**: no starter, no hints, no solution to peek at. The tests are exactly the ones you passed
Why: pulling something out of memory is what makes it stay there. Reading your old code feels like knowing
it; rebuilding it cold shows whether you do. If you get stuck, that is useful news: go back to the lesson,
then come back and try again tomorrow.
This check, plus the boss, is what proves the module.

steps.prompt: This merge counts its comparisons. What does it print?
steps.explain: Every left value is smaller than 4, so three comparisons empty the left side. The right side is then copied with no comparisons at all.

steps.title: Rebuild Merge cold
prompt: Write `int[] Merge(int[] l, int[] r)`: both inputs are sorted ascending; return a new sorted array with every item from both.
Use the two-finger technique, `O(n)`. No `Concat`, `OrderBy` or `Sort`.
**From memory this time:** the editor starts empty and the tests are the ones you passed in the lesson.
